annotation.title_clean: Impact of artificial intelligence on the financial sector
annotation.title_en: Impact of artificial intelligence on the financial sector
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union (C series)
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament resolution of 25 November 2025 on AI in the financial sector. It finds existing sectoral financial legislation largely sufficient, urges clarity on AI Act overlaps, proportionate supervision, guidance, sandboxes, and AI literacy, and warns against gold-plating and added complexity while balancing innovation with consumer protection and financial stability.
key_provisions_or_claims: Sectoral financial legislation is mainly sufficient; additional AI legislation would add complexity and avoid gold-plating.
Calls for Commission guidance on applying financial law and the AI Act, and for resolving overlaps in the Digital Omnibus.
Supports financial authorities as market surveillance bodies for high-risk AI (credit scoring, life/health insurance pricing).
Asks to assess DORA exit strategies for AI models hosted by third-party providers to address concentration risk.
Calls for AI regulatory sandboxes, AI literacy and upskilling, and human oversight of autonomous systems.
